Filename: Historical Map Delta Northern Section - 1886 Belden Atlas.jpg
Original Caption: This shows part of the northern end of town.  The development of these areas reflects the history of the area.  In 1808, the year that Abel Stevens Sr. sold his mills and northern portion of his downtown Delta property to William Jones, his son, Able Stevens Jr. set up a sawmill on what is called as Foundry Creek on this map, today's Cowans Creek.  His dam created what is shown as Hicocks Pond.  This business activity would have attracted some development to this part of town.

Filename: Historical Map Delta Downtown Core - 1886 Belden Atlas.jpg
Original Caption: This is a crop showing the downtown core.  This pre-dates the Jubilee Block, in 1892 it was the 3 storey high Singleton Block (which burned down 1896).  We have photos of the Singleton Block on our website.

Original Caption: Hazel Horton (?) in a canoe.  This is a AI recreation of a colourized version of the original photo scan (see next images).  Both the original b&w photo and a colourized version are very blurry, the face is not clear.  AI has recreated a face.  While not authentic, it does bring the original blurry photo to life.  When using AI, I (Ken) check to try to ensure that no new elements are added that would impact the heritage authenticity of the photo.

Filename: Hazel Horton Painting of Delta Mill Area c.1906.jpg
Original Caption: In this painting, done by Hazel Horton in about 1906, we see the very high stack of the boiler chimney.  The high height improved the draft of the boiler, making it more efficient.  It was installed by mill owner George Haskin in about 1898.  It allowed the mill and/or sawmill to operate in times of low water flow when the turbines weren't working.
